title: Fail closed and clean quality child processes
outOfScope: Changing quality gate membership, thresholds, or parallelism policy.
Changing application test behavior or suppressing quality failures.
Killing processes outside the quality session created by this Work Item.

sources.reason: quality-full currently launches fast and heavy phases without session-owned descendant cleanup.
Existing per-gate evidence writer establishes the session and process boundary context.
Existing quality ownership architecture tests are the correct regression location.

rawUserRequest: Continue. If a process issue is found during a Work Item, repair the process before proceeding. Quality evidence must be reliable and no old test process may remain to contaminate a retry.

declaredIntent.summary: Make each quality invocation own and terminate only its phase process group so failed attempts cannot contaminate later evidence.

riskAssessment.reason: A failed quality invocation must not retain test descendants that overwrite shared artifacts during retries.

executionDecision.reason: The user authorized process repairs before continuing governed delivery.

preReviewWarnings: Only the process group created for this quality phase may be terminated; unrelated processes must remain untouched.

checkpointPolicy.reason: Record at least one checkpoint before finishing to reduce mid-task drift.

acceptance: quality-full runs fast and heavy phases as separately owned process groups and waits for each phase result.
If any phase fails or the parent is interrupted, the helper terminates and reaps only that owned process group before returning failure.
The helper preserves the existing gate list, session/run/timing/log/JUnit bindings, and failure status; it does not turn a failed quality run into success.
Unit regressions prove success sequencing, failure cleanup, interruption cleanup, and Makefile integration; full quality then passes with one clean session.
guidelines: Terminate only process groups created by the quality-session helper and preserve unrelated processes.
Fail closed: preserve phase exit failures and diagnostics while ensuring no owned descendant remains.

intent.problem: A quality-fast failure returned an error while a project-test child from the same quality invocation remained alive. A retry then ran concurrently and shared coverage output, so neither session was reliable evidence.
constraints: Do not alter gate membership, thresholds, or parallelism.
Create a dedicated process group per fast/heavy phase.
Terminate and reap only the created group on failure or interruption.
Keep existing session artifact paths and provider-visible diagnostics.
intent.rationale: An explicit owned process group gives the quality parent a bounded cleanup target, preventing failed attempts from contaminating a retry without touching unrelated user processes.

restrictedWriteApproval.reason: User authorized process repairs and continued execution.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Fast phase failure terminates and reaps its owned group before the command returns failure.
scenarioCoverage.expected: No owned child remains and the original nonzero exit is returned.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Unit-test helper with controlled process mocks and run full quality.

scenarioCoverage.scenario: Fast success then heavy success preserves ordered execution and produces the ordinary session evidence.
scenarioCoverage.expected: Fast completes before heavy and exit is zero only when both succeed.
scenarioCoverage.verificationPlan: Unit-test order and Makefile integration, then run full quality.

rollbackNote: Revert this Work Item diff and restore related tests and docs.
